chunks: Muhammad ibn Muhammad narrated to me from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Umar ibn Yazid, and I do not know it except from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever says in his Witr prayer, when he prits Witr: 'I seek forgiveness of Allah and I repent to Him,' seventy times while standing, and persists in doing so until a year has passed for him, Allah will record him among those who seek forgiveness at dawn, and forgiveness will become obligatory for him from Allah, the Mighty and Sublime.

key_terms.أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيْهِ: I seek Allah's forgiveness and I repent to Him

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Istighfar seventy times in Witr prayer for a year?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith highlights the virtue of consistent *istighfar* during the Witr prayer, linking the supplicant to the righteous who seek forgiveness in the pre-dawn hours (*al-asr*). The promise that forgiveness becomes 'obligatory' (*wajabat*) upon Allah emphasizes the certainty of divine mercy for those who maintain this specific devotional discipline for a full year.
